nodes.statement: For each fixed d≥1, prove matching upper and lower asymptotic bounds over all n-element subsets of ℝ^d.
The determination standard is order of growth; matching leading constants are not required unless claimed as the answer.
For any source lower bound of the form ∃c>0 eventually ..., the constant c is fixed independently of n and 'eventually' means all sufficiently large n.
DETERMINATION CLOSE: determine the sharp asymptotic order of f_d(n) for every fixed integer d≥1, with exact or sharper results accepted.
No dimension or asymptotic regime may remain merely unknown.

METAMATHEMATICAL COMPLETE CLOSE: genuine independence/undecidability may replace a mathematical determination only when proved for the exact fixed-d order question and all remaining dimensions are exhausted.
Let $f_d(n)$ be minimal such that, in any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, there exist at most $f_d(n)$ pairs of points which distance $1$ apart. Estimate $f_d(n)$.

Θ(n²) for all d≥3 dies at d=3: unit-distance graphs in ℝ³ are K_{3,3}-free (any 3 points have ≤2 common unit-neighbors), so f₃(n) ≤ 2^{−2/3}n^{5/3}+O(n)=o(n²); repair = restrict to d≥4 (proved: ⌊n/2⌋⌈n/2⌉ ≤ f_d(n) ≤ C(n,2)) with f₁(n)=n−1 exact and d∈{2,3} order-open.
